description: Statutory edges. A charge not initiated by arrest, an offense date on the exact effectiveFrom boundary of January 1, 2018, an anticipated acquittal rather than a dismissal, and a participant represented by private counsel rather than a public defender. The synthetic date is a test input at the boundary, not an asserted fact about any record. Court identity and protected fields stay blank.

screeningAnswers.isRepresented: Yes — private counsel is on the case
screeningAnswers.offenseDateOnOrAfter2018: Yes — 01/01/2018, the exact first day of the window (synthetic boundary test value)
screeningAnswers.dismissalWithPrejudice: Not applicable — the anticipated disposition is an acquittal, not a dismissal

eligibilityData.waitingPeriodText: None, but the petition must be filed the same day, during the disposition hearing.
boundaryUnderTest: effectiveFrom edge: the subsection reaches acquittals and dismissals with prejudice on or after January 1, 2018. Records of offenses occurring before January 1, 2018 are excluded.
recordTypes edge: a charge not initiated by arrest, the second of the two record types on this track.

dispositions edge: acquittal, the branch on which the dismissalWithPrejudice screening key is not asked (the registry marks it conditional, "Asked because only acquittal or dismissal with prejudice is within the subsection").
Timing edge: the window is the hearing itself. There is no waiting period and no later filing window.
Exclusion edge, not exercised here: a dismissal without prejudice is not within the subsection.
Exclusion edge, not exercised here: minor traffic offenses under § 5.2(a)(3)(B).
additionalFacts: The petition must be filed with the circuit clerk on the same day and during the same hearing in which the case is disposed.
If the petition is not filed during the hearing, ordinary sealing under § 5.2(c)(3)(A) remains available at any time through il-seal-nonconv.

attachments: Proposed Order on Petition for Immediate Sealing (component il-immediate-seal-proposed-order-2, no outcome asserted)
